```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20211201)
set.seed(20211201)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Pastuszak_2021_testosteroneUndecanoate"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Pastuszak_2021_testosteroneUndecanoate"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.1939>

The model describes total serum testosterone after 750 mg intramuscular
testosterone undecanoate (Aveed) in men with hypogonadism. Testosterone
undecanoate is absorbed slowly from the oily intramuscular depot
(absorption half-life about 29 days at 101 kg), and the model adds an apparent
zero-order endogenous testosterone input into the central compartment:

$$R(t) = R_b e^{-K_1 t} + R_{ss}\left(1 - e^{-K_2 t}\right)$$

`R_b` (`kin_te`) is the predose production rate. It is switched off within
hours of the first injection (`K_1` = 10 1/h, fixed) and then recovers, with a
half-life of about 40 days, to the steady-state rate `R_ss` (`kin_te_ss`).

# Population

The model was fitted to 2360 total testosterone concentrations from 130 men
with hypogonadism in the phase 3, single-arm, open-label Study IP157-001 Part C
(NCT00467870), run at 31 US sites (Pastuszak 2021 Methods and Table 1). Mean
age was 54.2 years (range 24-75), mean weight 101.2 kg (SD 18.0), mean BMI
32.0 kg/m^2 and mean baseline SHBG 20.9 nmol/L (SD 8.9); 74.6% were White,
12.3% Black and 13.1% other races. Patients received 750 mg in 3 mL of castor
oil and benzyl benzoate into the buttock at baseline, week 4 and then every
10 weeks for up to 84 weeks. Sampling was dense across injection intervals 3
and 4 (weeks 14-34). The 117-patient original-study PK population (mean
weight 101.6 kg, SD 17.4; mean SHBG 20.8 nmol/L, SD 8.5) was the template for
the paper's simulations.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Pastuszak_2021_testosteroneUndecanoate"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (Ka at 101 kg) | 0.001 1/h | Table 2 (units printed 'L/h') |
| `lcl` (CL/F at 101 kg, SHBG 20 nmol/L) | 197 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (V/F at 101 kg) | 12 300 L | Table 2 |
| `lkin_te` (Rb) | 0.445 mg/h | Table 2 |
| `lkin_te_ss` (Rss) | 0.572 mg/h | Table 2 |
| `lk_suppression_te` (K1) | 10 1/h, fixed | Table 2 (units printed 'L/h') |
| `lk_recovery_te` (K2) | 0.000727 1/h | Table 2 (units printed 'L/h') |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75, fixed | Table 2 |
| `e_sex_hormone_binding_globulin_cl` | -0.219 | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_ka` | -1.83 | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1, fixed | Table 2 |
| Reference covariate values | 101 kg, 20 nmol/L | Table 2 footnote b |
| `etalcl` | 0.0392 (20.0% CV) | Table 2; `log(CV^2 + 1)` |
| `etalka` | 0.2004 (47.1% CV) | Table 2; `log(CV^2 + 1)` |
| No IIV on V/F | n/a | Results ('The model did not support estimation of interindividual variability on V/F') |
| `propSd` | 0.188 | Table 2 |
| `addSd` | 56.8 ng/dL | Table 2 |
| Structure: 1 compartment, first-order absorption and elimination | n/a | Results; Figure 1 |
| `R(t)` endogenous input equation | n/a | Results, equation following Figure 1 |
| Covariate forms: power models centred on the reference values | n/a | Methods (Population PK Modeling); Table 2 |
| `central(0) <- kin_te / kel` | n/a | Assumed: predose endogenous steady state (see Assumptions) |
| `Cc <- central / vc * 1e5` (mg/L to ng/dL) | n/a | Unit conversion; concentrations in ng/dL throughout |

# Virtual cohort

Observed data are not public. As in the paper, each regimen is simulated in a
cohort of 117 men whose covariates follow the PK population in Table 1. The
same 117 covariate sets are used for both regimens. Weight is normal
(mean 101.6 kg, SD 17.4) with a floor of 65 kg, the study's PK-population
inclusion threshold. SHBG is log-normal with mean 20.8 nmol/L and SD 8.5.

Dosing is 750 mg at week 0, at week 4, and then every 10 weeks (approved) or
every 8 weeks (alternative), through dose 10. As in the paper, concentrations
are sampled every 48 hours.

```{r cohort}
n_sub <- 117L
h_per_week <- 168

cov <- tibble(
  sub = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmax(65, rnorm(n_sub, 101.6, 17.4)),
  SEX_HORMONE_BINDING_GLOBULIN = {
    sdl <- sqrt(log(1 + (8.5 / 20.8)^2))
    exp(rnorm(n_sub, log(20.8) - sdl^2 / 2, sdl))
  }
)

dose_weeks <- function(tau_weeks) c(0, 4, 4 + tau_weeks * (1:8))

make_cohort <- function(tau_weeks, id_offset) {
  dose_t <- dose_weeks(tau_weeks) * h_per_week
  end_t <- dose_t[10] + tau_weeks * h_per_week
  obs_t <- seq(0, end_t, by = 48)
  per_sub <- function(i) {
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      tibble(time = dose_t, amt = 750, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
      tibble(time = obs_t, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
    ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        id = id_offset + i,
        WT = cov$WT[i],
        SEX_HORMONE_BINDING_GLOBULIN = cov$SEX_HORMONE_BINDING_GLOBULIN[i]
      )
  }
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), per_sub)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = paste0("Q", tau_weeks, "W"), tau_weeks = tau_weeks) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_cohort(10, id_offset = 0L),
  make_cohort(8, id_offset = 1000L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Pastuszak_2021_testosteroneUndecanoate")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("regimen", "tau_weeks")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

The paper's simulated exposure metrics include residual variability, so the
per-patient Cmax, Cavg and Ctrough below are computed from the `sim` column (the
prediction with residual error added), not from `Cc` (the individual
prediction).

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2: concentration-time profile under the approved regimen

Figure 2 of the paper is a prediction-corrected VPC of the observed data. The
observations are not public, so the plot below shows the simulated median and
95% prediction interval for the approved regimen over the same 0-74 week
window. It reproduces the paper's shape: a predose baseline near 230 ng/dL, a
drop then rise over the first two injections, peaks near 1000 ng/dL after each
injection, and troughs that rise slowly as endogenous production recovers.

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "Q10W", time <= 74 * h_per_week) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    lo = quantile(sim, 0.025),
    med = median(sim),
    hi = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / h_per_week, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (week)", y = "Total testosterone (ng/dL)",
    title = "Simulated median and 95% prediction interval, 750 mg every 10 weeks",
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 2 of Pastuszak 2021 (simulated data only)."
  )
```

## Typical-value check against Table 4

Typical-value Cavg after dose 10 depends only on clearance, dose and the
endogenous input, so it tests the structural model, the dose and the units
directly. It is computed for a 101 kg patient with SHBG 20 nmol/L. Only
Cavg is compared here: the paper's Cmax and Ctrough include residual error,
which shifts them away from the typical-value prediction.

```{r typical}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
# One single-subject solve per regimen for the typical patient.
solve_typical <- function(tau_weeks) {
  ev <- make_cohort(tau_weeks, id_offset = 0L) |>
    dplyr::filter(id == 1) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = 101, SEX_HORMONE_BINDING_GLOBULIN = 20)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev, keep = c("regimen", "tau_weeks")) |>
    as.data.frame()
}
sim_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(solve_typical(10), solve_typical(8))

typ_cavg <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, tau_weeks) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cavg = {
      start <- dose_weeks(tau_weeks[1])[10] * h_per_week
      end <- start + tau_weeks[1] * h_per_week
      keep <- time >= start & time <= end
      tt <- time[keep]
      cc <- Cc[keep]
      sum(diff(tt) * (head(cc, -1) + tail(cc, -1)) / 2) / (end - start)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(published = c(Q10W = 510.1, Q8W = 564.5)[regimen])

typ_cavg |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cavg / published - 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Typical-value Cavg (ng/dL)" = cavg,
    "Table 4 median Cavg (ng/dL)" = published,
    "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-tau_weeks) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value Cavg after dose 10 vs. Pastuszak 2021 Table 4.")

# Predose baseline is the endogenous steady state Rb / CL.
baseline_typ <- sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time == 0 & sim_typ$regimen == "Q10W"][1]
baseline_closed <- 0.445 / 197 * 1e5

cavg_ratio <- typ_cavg$cavg[typ_cavg$regimen == "Q8W"] /
  typ_cavg$cavg[typ_cavg$regimen == "Q10W"]

stopifnot(
  # Solve against its own closed form: numerical error only.
  abs(baseline_typ / baseline_closed - 1) < 1e-4,
  # Deterministic; realised +1.2% (Q10W) and +1.5% (Q8W). A wrong dose,
  # clearance or unit conversion moves Cavg by tens of percent.
  all(abs(typ_cavg$cavg / typ_cavg$published - 1) < 0.05),
  # Table 4 Cavg ratio 1.11; realised 1.109 (deterministic).
  abs(cavg_ratio - 1.11) < 0.03
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Cmax, Cavg and Ctrough are computed per patient for each dosing interval with
PKNCA, using the `sim` concentrations sampled every 48 hours. The paper defines
Ctrough as the last observed concentration in the dosing interval before the
next dose, which is PKNCA's `clast.obs`. Dose 1 covers weeks 0-4, so its
interval is 4 weeks for both regimens.

```{r pknca}
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, regimen)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id)

interval_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(10, 8), function(tau) {
  dt <- dose_weeks(tau) * h_per_week
  tibble(
    regimen = paste0("Q", tau, "W"),
    dose_number = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 10),
    start = dt[c(1, 2, 3, 4, 10)],
    end = c(dt[2], dt[c(3, 4, 5)], dt[10] + tau * h_per_week)
  )
}))

intervals <- interval_tbl |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, start, end) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmax = TRUE, cav = TRUE, clast.obs = TRUE) |>
  as.data.frame()

run_nca <- function(sim_df) {
  # Residual error can push a few low simulated observations below zero; an
  # assay cannot report a negative concentration, so they are floored at 0.
  sim_nca <- sim_df |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(sim)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(sim, 0)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)
  # Linear trapezoids: Cavg is the time-average of the 48-hour samples.
  nca_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    conc_obj, dose_obj,
    intervals = intervals,
    options = list(auc.method = "linear")
  )
  out <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(nca_data)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(interval_tbl, by = c("regimen", "start", "end"))
  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(out$dose_number),
    !anyNA(out$PPORRES[out$PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cav", "clast.obs")])
  )
  out
}

nca_long <- run_nca(sim)
```

## Comparison against Table 4 (dose 10)

Table 4 reports, for each exposure metric, the median over 500 simulated
studies of the per-study median. In the table below, Ctrough is the row
labelled Clast (PKNCA's `clast.obs`).

```{r nca_compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cmax, ~cav, ~clast.obs,
  "Q8W", 978.2, 564.5, 391.3,
  "Q10W", 934.2, 510.1, 351.9
)

sim_dose10 <- nca_long |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_number == 10, PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cav", "clast.obs")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_dose10,
  reference = published,
  by = "regimen",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/dL", cav = "ng/dL", clast.obs = "ng/dL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs. Pastuszak 2021 Table 4 (dose 10). * differs from reference by >20%."
)

med10 <- sim_dose10 |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(published, -regimen, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("regimen", "PPTESTCD")
  )
stopifnot(nrow(med10) == 6L)
med10
stopifnot(
  # Cavg is structural (dose, CL, endogenous input); realised within 2%.
  all(abs(med10$med[med10$PPTESTCD == "cav"] / med10$ref[med10$PPTESTCD == "cav"] - 1) < 0.10),
  # Cmax and Ctrough of one 117-patient cohort, also shifted by the rounding
  # of Ka in Table 2 (see Assumptions): realised within 10%. A wrong dose,
  # volume or unit moves them by far more than 25%.
  all(abs(med10$med / med10$ref - 1) < 0.25)
)
```

Simulated Cavg agrees with Table 4 to within a few percent for both regimens.
Median Cmax tends to come out low (about 5-10%) and median Ctrough high (up to
about 10%). That is the pattern expected if Ka is slightly too small, and
Table 2 prints Ka to only one significant figure (see the sensitivity run
below).

## Percentage of patients within the prespecified ranges (Table 5 and Table S1)

```{r ranges}
range_summary <- function(nca_df) {
  nca_df |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cav", "clast.obs")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, dose_number, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, dose_number) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Cavg 300-1000` = 100 * mean(cav >= 300 & cav <= 1000),
    `Cavg <300` = 100 * mean(cav < 300),
    `Cavg >1000` = 100 * mean(cav > 1000),
    `Cmax <1500` = 100 * mean(cmax < 1500),
    `Cmax 1800-2500` = 100 * mean(cmax >= 1800 & cmax <= 2500),
    `Cmax >2500` = 100 * mean(cmax > 2500),
    `Ctrough >300` = 100 * mean(clast.obs > 300),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(regimen, dose_number), names_to = "metric", values_to = "simulated")
}
range_tbl <- range_summary(nca_long)

# Table S1 (doses 1-4) and Table 5 (dose 10); medians across 500 simulated studies.
pub_ranges <- tibble::tribble(
  ~metric, ~dose_number, ~Q10W, ~Q8W,
  "Cavg 300-1000", 1, 70.1, 70.1,
  "Cavg 300-1000", 2, 92.3, 94.0,
  "Cavg 300-1000", 3, 96.6, 97.4,
  "Cavg 300-1000", 4, 97.4, 98.3,
  "Cavg 300-1000", 10, 97.4, 98.3,
  "Cavg <300", 1, 29.9, 29.9,
  "Cavg <300", 2, 7.7, 6.0,
  "Cavg <300", 3, 3.4, 1.7,
  "Cavg <300", 4, 2.6, 0.9,
  "Cavg <300", 10, 1.7, 0.9,
  "Cavg >1000", 1, 0.0, 0.0,
  "Cavg >1000", 2, 0.0, 0.0,
  "Cavg >1000", 3, 0.0, 0.0,
  "Cavg >1000", 4, 0.0, 0.9,
  "Cavg >1000", 10, 0.0, 0.9,
  "Cmax <1500", 1, 98.3, 98.3,
  "Cmax <1500", 2, 92.3, 92.3,
  "Cmax <1500", 3, 92.3, 92.3,
  "Cmax <1500", 4, 91.5, 90.6,
  "Cmax <1500", 10, 90.6, 88.9,
  "Cmax 1800-2500", 1, 0.9, 0.9,
  "Cmax 1800-2500", 2, 1.7, 2.6,
  "Cmax 1800-2500", 3, 2.6, 2.6,
  "Cmax 1800-2500", 4, 2.6, 3.4,
  "Cmax 1800-2500", 10, 3.0, 3.4,
  "Cmax >2500", 1, 0.0, 0.0,
  "Cmax >2500", 2, 0.0, 0.0,
  "Cmax >2500", 3, 0.0, 0.0,
  "Cmax >2500", 4, 0.0, 0.0,
  "Cmax >2500", 10, 0.0, 0.0,
  "Ctrough >300", 1, 51.3, 51.3,
  "Ctrough >300", 2, 53.0, 59.8,
  "Ctrough >300", 3, 63.2, 70.1,
  "Ctrough >300", 4, 65.8, 74.4,
  "Ctrough >300", 10, 66.7, 76.1
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Q10W, Q8W), names_to = "regimen", values_to = "published")

range_cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(pub_ranges, range_tbl, by = c("metric", "dose_number", "regimen"))
stopifnot(nrow(range_cmp) == nrow(pub_ranges))

range_cmp |>
  dplyr::arrange(regimen, dose_number) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Dose" = dose_number,
    "Metric (ng/dL)" = metric,
    "Published (%)" = published,
    "Simulated (%)" = simulated
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Percentage of patients within each range: Pastuszak 2021 Table S1 (doses 1-4) and Table 5 (dose 10) vs. one simulated 117-patient cohort per regimen.")

cavg_in <- range_cmp |>
  dplyr::filter(metric == "Cavg 300-1000", dose_number >= 3)
stopifnot(
  # Paper 96.6-98.3% from dose 3 on; a mis-scaled model drops this far
  # below 85%.
  all(cavg_in$simulated > 85)
)
```

From dose 2 onwards the Cavg categories match the published percentages
closely. Three quantities differ, and all are explained by the rounding of Ka
(next section). After dose 1, fewer simulated patients reach a Cavg of
300-1000 ng/dL (about 50-60% against 70.1%), because absorption from the first
injection is slower. From dose 2 onwards the share with Ctrough above
300 ng/dL runs up to about 12 points higher than published, and the share with
Cmax below 1500 ng/dL up to about 8 points higher.

## Sensitivity to the rounding of Ka

Table 2 prints Ka as 0.001 1/h (bootstrap 95% CI 0.001 to 0.002), so any
estimate from 0.0005 to 0.0015 would print the same way. The packaged model
keeps the printed 0.001. The run below repeats the simulation on the same
virtual cohort with Ka = 0.0014 1/h. Faster absorption raises the early
(dose 1) exposure and the dose-10 peaks and lowers the dose-10 troughs, which
moves every quantity that disagrees above towards the published value, while
Cavg after dose 3 is unchanged.

```{r ka-sensitivity}
mod_ka <- rxode2::ini(mod, lka = log(0.0014))
sim_ka <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ka, events = events, keep = c("regimen", "tau_weeks")) |>
  as.data.frame()
nca_ka <- run_nca(sim_ka)

ka_medians <- nca_ka |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_number == 10, PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "clast.obs")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ka_0.0014 = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(metric = paste("Median", ifelse(PPTESTCD == "cmax", "Cmax", "Ctrough"), "(ng/dL), dose 10")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    med10 |> dplyr::select(regimen, PPTESTCD, ka_0.001 = med, published = ref),
    by = c("regimen", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, metric, published, ka_0.001, ka_0.0014)

ka_ranges <- range_summary(nca_ka) |>
  dplyr::rename(ka_0.0014 = simulated) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(range_cmp, by = c("regimen", "dose_number", "metric")) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    (metric == "Cavg 300-1000" & dose_number == 1) |
      (metric %in% c("Cmax <1500", "Ctrough >300") & dose_number == 10)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(metric = paste0(metric, " (%), dose ", dose_number)) |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, metric, published, ka_0.001 = simulated, ka_0.0014)

dplyr::bind_rows(ka_medians, ka_ranges) |>
  dplyr::arrange(regimen, metric) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Quantity" = metric,
    "Published" = published,
    "Ka 0.001 (packaged)" = ka_0.001,
    "Ka 0.0014 (sensitivity)" = ka_0.0014
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Exposure quantities most sensitive to Ka: published values vs. the packaged Ka and Ka = 0.0014 1/h, on the same virtual cohort.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Ka precision.** Table 2 prints Ka to one significant figure (0.001 1/h).
  The packaged model uses that printed value. With it, simulated Cavg from
  dose 2 onwards matches Tables 4, 5 and S1. But median Cmax runs low, median
  Ctrough and the share with Ctrough above 300 ng/dL run high, and too few
  patients reach the Cavg range after dose 1. Ka = 0.0014 1/h, which also
  prints as 0.001, moves all of these to the published values. The
  maintainers checked this in a 600-patient run: dose-1 Cavg 300-1000 ng/dL
  in 74.5% of patients (published 70.1%), and dose-10 Ctrough above 300 ng/dL
  in 67.0% (published 66.7%) for the 10-week regimen. The maintainers did
  not tune Ka, because the unrounded estimate is not published.
- **Dose amount.** The dose is entered as 750 mg of testosterone undecanoate,
  the labelled amount, with no conversion to testosterone equivalents
  (474 mg). The paper does not state the dose unit used in the dataset.
  With 750 mg, typical-value Cavg after dose 10 matches Table 4 to within 2%
  for both regimens. The testosterone-equivalent dose would give a Cavg near
  430 ng/dL. Because CL/F and V/F are apparent parameters, this choice is
  absorbed into F.
- **Initial condition.** The paper does not print the initial condition.
  The central compartment starts at the predose endogenous steady state,
  `central(0) = Rb / kel` (226 ng/dL for the typical patient). With K1 fixed
  at 10 1/h, Rb is gone within hours of the first dose. Rb could therefore
  only have been estimated (8.5% RSE) through the predose baseline it sets,
  and the Figure 2 VPC median near 230 ng/dL at week 0 agrees.
- **Time origin.** The paper's `TIME` in the R(t) equation is taken as time
  since the first injection.
- **Rate-constant units.** Table 2 prints the units of Ka, K1 and K2 as 'L/h'.
  They are first-order rate constants, and are encoded in 1/h.
- **IIV scale.** IIV is reported as %CV. It is converted with
  `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)`. Reading the %CV as `100 * omega` instead would
  give 0.0400 for CL/F and 0.222 for Ka.
- **Residual error.** The additive term labelled 'SE' in Table 2
  (56.8 ng/dL) is taken as the residual standard deviation.
- **Concentration units.** Amounts are in mg and volumes in L; `Cc` is
  converted from mg/L to ng/dL by multiplying by 1e5.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight is drawn as normal with a 65 kg floor and SHBG as
  log-normal, using the Table 1 means and SDs. The paper's simulations reused
  the actual covariates of the 117 PK-population patients, which are not
  published. Each regimen is simulated as one 117-patient study, not as 500
  studies.
- **Inconsistency within the paper.** For the dose-3 Cavg categories,
  Table 3's simulated column (94.0 / 6.0 / 0.0%) disagrees with Table S1
  (96.6 / 3.4 / 0.0% for the 10-week regimen). Table 3's simulated column is
  also identical to its observed column, so the comparison above uses Table S1.
- **Covariates screened but not retained.** Age, albumin, BMI and race were
  tested and not retained. They are recorded in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded` metadata.
- **Errata.** No correction notice was found as of 2026-10-04.
